Attempt 16 (this cycle): resolved fix-request-review-004's 1 major finding (mutable-reference isolation, AC9/AC10). Root cause: RequestContext.run()/CorrelationContext.run() bound the caller-supplied store object directly into the nested CLS frame's namespace slot; if the caller passed the parent's own currently-active store reference back in (e.g. `run(this.get()!, ...)`), or a shallow copy still aliasing the parent's roles/permissions arrays, mutations made inside the nested callback were visible on the parent's object after the nested call returned (success and throw paths both affected). Fix: both facades now call `RuntimeContextAccessor.isActive()` before opening the nested frame, and whenever a parent is already active, bind an isolated clone of the store (new cloneRequestContextStore() helper for RequestContextStore — new object plus new roles/permissions arrays; inline `{ ...store }` for the flat CorrelationStore) instead of the caller's reference. When no parent is active, the original reference is still bound directly and uncloned, preserving the pre-existing `expect(requestContext.get()).toBe(store)` characterization test for the non-nested path. Added 5 new regression tests (3 in request-context.spec.ts: same-reference nested run() on success/throw, shallow-copy-aliased-roles/permissions; 2 in correlation-context.spec.ts: same-reference nested run() on success/throw). Also fixed the accompanying AC21 finding: ai/domains/request-context/overview.md's SYSTEM_ACTOR_ID/isSystemActor terminology table incorrectly grouped CLI/worker/scheduler together as all receiving SYSTEM_ACTOR_ID — corrected to match the accurate per-transport semantics already in request-context.ts's code comments (only CLI runAsSystem() sets isSystemActor; worker has no RequestContextStore at all; scheduler has no consumer). Root cause: claimValueOwnership() only walked plain objects/arrays (isTraversableContainer) and treated everything else (any class instance, Map, Set, function) as an implicitly safe, unwalked leaf, while a walked plain object/array's own symbol-keyed and non-enumerable/accessor properties were skipped entirely by Object.values — reproduced by the reviewer as two distinct Box class instances, and separately two distinct plain objects sharing a nested reference under a Symbol key, each pair smuggling a shared mutable reference past ownership claiming and leaking a mutation between two concurrently-opened roots. Fix: ownership claiming in libs/platform/context/src/runtime-context.types.ts is now a closed-world preflight validator — a new assertSupportedContainerShape() rejects any symbol-keyed or non-enumerable/accessor own property on a walked plain object/array, and collectOwnableNodes() now rejects (synchronously, before either seed's runRoot() runs) any non-traversable value that is not a Date or explicitly opted in via the new exported markRuntimeContextValueAtomic(value) — the deliberate, documented escape hatch for a genuinely non-cloneable infrastructure reference (e.g. a TypeORM QueryRunner), which no production call site currently needs since QueryRunner is always bound via setNamespace() after runRoot(), never through RuntimeContextSeed.set(). Claiming is also now transactional: collectOwnableNodes() validates the complete graph into a local set before claimValueOwnership() commits it to the shared seededValues WeakSet, so a rejected graph never leaves an unrelated, individually-valid sibling node permanently claimed. 10 new regression tests added to runtime-context.service.spec.ts's new 'unsupported value-graph shapes are rejected before any root opens' describe block (45 cases total, up from 35); the pre-existing 'claims ownership of an atomic non-cloneable instance' test was updated to call markRuntimeContextValueAtomic() explicitly instead of relying on the old implicit any-class-instance-is-safe behavior.
